issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may determine whether a writ petitioner has locus standi and whether the petition is maintainable even when that issue was not urged before the High Court.
material_facts: The appellant was named as a party to the writ proceeding but did not appear because he said notice had not been served on him.
The appellant raised the petitioner’s lack of locus standi and the petition’s maintainability in the appeal, although the point had not been urged before the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court had jurisdiction in the appeal to determine the petitioner’s locus standi and whether the writ petition was maintainable.
issues.legal_principle: An appellate court may examine the soundness of the decision and determine threshold matters such as the competence of the appeal, a party’s locus standi, and the maintainability of the petition, including a point not raised below. The Court relied on Ebrahim Aboobakar v. Custodian General of Evacuee Property.

predicates.appellate_proceeding: The matter is before a court in an appeal from a lower court’s decision.
predicates.threshold_maintainability_issue_raised_o: A party asks the appellate court to decide whether the proceeding or a party’s participation in it is competent or maintainable.
predicates.threshold_maintainability_issue_not_urge: The maintainability issue was not presented for decision in the lower court.

issues.definition: When an appeal raises a maintainability issue that was not urged below, the appellate court may decide that issue.

issues.legal_issue: An ordinary writ petition is not maintainable by a petitioner whose asserted personal right is not affected by the challenged action, absent an applicable exceptional basis for standing.
material_facts: The petitioner challenged a mining lease granted to another party, alleging that the leased area included the area for which he had applied.
The petitioner’s application was not for any part of the area covered by the other party’s lease, so he had no interest in the subject matter of that lease.
The petitioner relied on an alleged direct infringement of his own right and was neither a party to nor a person aggrieved or affected by the grant.
issues.conclusion: The petitioner had no locus standi, and the writ petition was not maintainable.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 226, the existence of a right affected by the challenged action ordinarily grounds the court’s jurisdiction; the relevant right is ordinarily the petitioner’s personal or individual right. A proprietary interest is not essential if another personal interest is affected, and exceptional cases may permit a prejudicially affected person without a proprietary or fiduciary interest to seek relief. The rule may be relaxed for writs such as habeas corpus or quo warranto. For a stranger, intervention may depend on the nature and extent of the asserted interest and whether the public interest calls for intervention, and ultimately rests in the court’s discretion. The Court relied on Chiranjit Lal Chowdhuri v. Union of India, State of Orissa v. Madan Gopal Rungta, Calcutta Gas Company v. State of West Bengal, Godde Venkateswara Rao v. Government of Andhra Pradesh, and R. v. Thames Magistrates’ Court, ex parte Greenbaum.

rule.if: ordinary_writ_proceeding and petitioner_asserts_personal_right and asserted_right_not_affected and petitioner_not_party_or_affected and no_exceptional_basis_for_stranger_standing

predicates.ordinary_writ_proceeding: The proceeding is an ordinary application for a constitutional writ, rather than a proceeding such as habeas corpus or quo warranto.
predicates.petitioner_asserts_personal_right: The petitioner seeks relief on the basis that the challenged action directly infringed the petitioner’s own right.
predicates.asserted_right_not_affected: The facts show that the challenged action did not affect the right the petitioner asserted.
predicates.petitioner_not_party_or_affected: The petitioner was neither a party to the relevant subject matter nor a person aggrieved or otherwise affected by the challenged action.
predicates.no_exceptional_basis_for_stranger_standi: The circumstances do not provide an exceptional basis, such as a public-interest reason for intervention, to permit a stranger to seek relief.

issues.definition: If an ordinary writ petitioner asserts a personal right that was not affected, is not a party or otherwise affected, and has no exceptional basis for standing, the petitioner lacks locus standi and the petition is not maintainable.
